source.title: Initialization is Critical to Whether Transformers Fit Composite Functions by Reasoning or Memorizing
source.authors: Zhongwang Zhang; Peng-Xiao Lin; Zhiwei Wang; Yaoyu Zhang; Zhi-Qin John Xu

record.tranche_reason: The study varies initialization and weight decay and evaluates generalization and solution type, bearing conceptually on initialization-dependent generalization and the efficiency account. It does not reproduce grokking’s delayed-accuracy trajectory.
record.gate_note: The paper reports initialization-dependent inferential versus symmetric solutions, generalization comparisons, and training/perplexity results. It does not report training accuracy saturating before a delayed test-accuracy rise. The authors’ references to grokking are background, not results. Perplexity results on SlimPajama are recorded as related findings, not evidence of delayed generalization.
record.test_reason: The paper never measures delayed generalization: no curve shows training accuracy saturating before test accuracy rises. It does bear on two versions in a new setting, an anchor-function compositional task plus GPT-2 on SCAN, COGS, PrOntoQA and addition. For V6, identical training data produce mechanistically different solutions (inferential vs symmetric) depending on initialization scale. For V5, smaller initialization and larger weight decay favour a low-complexity generalizing solution over memorization.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that initialization scale determines whether transformers learn inferential (compositional) or symmetric (memorizing) solutions. They tie inferential solutions to a low-complexity bias and report that small initialization and larger weight decay improve generalization on GPT-2 and real datasets. They also propose the initialization rate gamma as a tunable hyperparameter.
record.recipe_differences: The study varies initialization scale and weight decay on composite-function and other tasks, and measures solution type and generalization. It does not use the original grokking setup to measure delayed generalization after overfitting.
record.method_sensitivity: Initialization scale, model depth, learning rate, weight-decay coefficient, and dataset size affect reported solution or generalization outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: GPT-2 Medium trained for 40B tokens on SlimPajama reaches lower perplexity with smaller initialization, on both the GitHub and GitHub+Wikipedia compositions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Smaller initialization scale improves language-model perplexity in pretraining.

fits_no_version.finding: Large initialization with deep models fails even on seen anchors, memorizing individual data points.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Very large initialization produces pure memorization without generalization to the data split.

record.code_released: The paper says code is provided in the attached file; no URL stated.
record.problems: The central phase-diagram results are presented mainly as figures and qualitative trends, with accuracy values not stated in the text. The paper reports four-run standard deviations for GPT-2 in Fig. 2(c), but gives few numerical comparisons for the other settings. The authors note that much of the analysis uses synthetic data and that further verification on a wider range of models is needed.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible reported results were left out.

untested.parts: No train-then-delayed-test accuracy trajectory; no delay versus training-set size.
No progress measures anticipating a jump; no removal of memorizing components over training. Fig. 12(b) shows complexity growing gradually, but it is not tied to any delayed accuracy rise.
No grokking-like delay is measured on any dataset. Initialization shifts which solution is learned, not the timing of generalization, and no lazy-to-rich delay transition is shown.
SlimPajama runs report perplexity only; no delayed generalization is measured.
No critical dataset size is identified and ungrokking below it is not tested. Circuit efficiency is proxied by condensation and rank, not by weight norm.
Optimizer and numerical artifacts are not examined.

missing.what: Weight decay and learning rate varied at fixed gamma=0.5: larger weight decay and learning rate raise inferential accuracy on the unseen pair. This is the unconfounded weight-decay evidence for V5.
Mechanistic evidence that the symmetric and inferential solutions are different algorithms (information flow, t-SNE, cosine similarity of fused vectors).
Condensation and low-rank structure of the small-initialization (generalizing) solution versus the large-initialization one.

record.verdict_notes: Grokking appears only in related work, and no delayed-generalization dynamics are reported. The V3 links on R5-R11 were removed because the version requires a delay. The V5 support rests on generalization versus memorization under a low-norm bias, not on grokking timing. The V6 challenge holds for this compositional task; whether it transfers to modular-arithmetic grokking is not shown.

versions.untested_parts: No small algorithmic dataset experiment reports training accuracy saturating followed by a long-delayed rise in test accuracy, or how that delay changes with training-set size.

The paper analyzes inferential and symmetric mechanisms and reports gradual growth in model complexity, but does not test whether memorizing components are later removed or whether continuous circuit measures anticipate a grokking accuracy jump.

Tests effects of initialization and weight decay on solution type and generalization, including on SCAN, COGS, PrOntoQA, and addition. It does not establish grokking-like delayed generalization on these datasets or a lazy-to-rich transition.
SlimPajama pretraining results report perplexity, not delayed generalization during realistic large-model pretraining or fine-tuning.

Tests whether initialization and weight decay affect reasoning/generalization and reports dataset-size trends on PrOntoQA. It does not establish a critical dataset size for grokking, ungrokking below it, or directly measure a low-norm generalizing circuit.

Tests whether initialization changes the learned solution on the same synthetic task. It does not establish that all other architectures and hyperparameter settings converge to different identifiable algorithms.
Does not test adaptive-optimizer instabilities or floating-point limits in the softmax as explanations for grokking.

relation.reason: Its own initialization sweeps and mechanism analyses directly test V6, although they do not demonstrate delayed generalization.

tranche.reason: The initialization-dependent, mechanistically distinct solutions provide a counterexample to V6's unrestricted algorithm-invariance claim, fitting T5's results requiring a version to be restated.

source_check.notes: The phase diagrams select the best of nine learning rates separately for each mapping, then average across three seeds. No train-saturation/test-rise grokking delay is demonstrated; endpoint evidence should remain distinct from a test of the efficiency mechanism.

statements.correction: SCAN and COGS: better compositional generalization with jointly small initialization and large decay; PrOntoQA: faster convergence and better hierarchical-relationship test accuracy; addition: better rule generalization with small initialization or large decay; no grokking-delay measurement.
statements.problem: PrOntoQA is not explicitly evaluated as an OOD split, and the addition result is stated for small initialization or large decay. These endpoints do not directly measure efficient-circuit selection.
